content.user_title: Build Java Anomaly Detection with Azure AI
content.value_statement: Java teams need reliable patterns for detecting unusual time-series behavior. This skill provides Azure AI Anomaly Detector examples for clients, models, inference, and errors.
actual_capabilities: Shows Maven dependency setup for the Azure AI Anomaly Detector Java package.
Demonstrates client creation with AzureKeyCredential and DefaultAzureCredential.
Explains univariate batch detection, last-point detection, and change point detection.
Covers multivariate model training, batch inference, last-point detection, and model deletion.
Provides Java error handling patterns for HttpResponseException.
limitations: Requires an Azure Anomaly Detector resource and valid credentials.
Uses documentation examples, not a complete runnable application.
Does not prepare, clean, or validate time-series datasets.
References a beta SDK version, so APIs may change.

use_cases.title: Add Batch Detection
use_cases.description: Use univariate detection patterns to flag unusual values in daily or hourly business metrics.

use_cases.title: Train Multivariate Models
use_cases.description: Build training and inference flows for correlated signals stored in Azure Blob Storage.

use_cases.title: Prototype Monitoring Logic
use_cases.description: Compare sensitivity, granularity, and result interpretation before adding anomaly alerts to services.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to create Azure AI Anomaly Detector Java clients using environment variables for endpoint and key.

prompt_templates.title: Detect a Series
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me adapt the univariate batch detection example for daily transaction counts with sensitivity guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multivariate Inference
prompt_templates.prompt: Outline the Java steps for training a multivariate model and running batch inference from Azure Blob Storage.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my anomaly detection design for credentials, data granularity, polling, error handling, and model lifecycle risks.

output_examples.input: A Java service needs daily batch anomaly detection for sales totals.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends univariate entire-series detection, daily granularity, sensitivity tuning, result checks, and Azure SDK exception handling.

output_examples.input: A monitoring team wants correlated sensor analysis from Blob Storage.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines multivariate training data setup, model training, batch inference, result polling, and contributor review.

output_examples.input: A developer needs safer Azure credential setup.
output_examples.output: The skill points to environment variables and DefaultAzureCredential patterns instead of storing secrets in source files.

best_practices: Load endpoints, keys, and SAS tokens from secure configuration, not source files.
Match time granularity to the real sampling interval before tuning sensitivity.
Handle Azure SDK errors and long-running model operations explicitly.
anti_patterns: Do not commit real API keys, endpoints, or SAS tokens into examples or repositories.
Do not train multivariate models on poorly aligned or missing time-series data.
Do not treat anomaly scores as final decisions without business validation.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Java applications that call Azure AI Anomaly Detector for time-series anomaly detection.

faq.question: Does it support univariate detection?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers batch detection, last-point detection, and change point detection for single time-series data.

faq.question: Does it support multivariate detection?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers model training, batch inference, last-point inference, result review, and model management.

faq.question: Are Azure credentials required?
faq.answer: Yes. Users need an Azure endpoint and authentication through an API key or Azure identity.

faq.question: Is this a complete application template?
faq.answer: No. It is a focused SDK guide with code patterns that developers adapt to their applications.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
